senses.meaning: a braid or bundle of fibre or other porous material (now generally twisted or woven cotton) in a candle, kerosene heater, oil lamp, etc.
examples: Trim the wick fairly short, so that the flame does not smoke.

senses.label: Verb
senses.meaning: of a material (especially a textile): to convey or draw off (liquid) by capillary action
examples: The fabric wicks perspiration away from the body.

senses.label: Chiefly followed
senses.meaning: chiefly followed by through or up: of a liquid: to move by capillary action through a porous material
examples: The moisture slowly wicked through the wood.

senses.label: Become wide or wider
senses.meaning: to become wide or wider
examples: His eyes widened as her negligee fell to the floor.

senses.label: Let out clothes
senses.meaning: to let out clothes to a larger size
examples: She widened his trousers for him.

senses.label: Move with irregular
senses.meaning: to move with irregular, back and forward or side to side motions, to shake or jiggle
examples: Her hips wiggle as she walks.
The jelly wiggles on the plate when you move it.

senses.label: Move with shaking or jiggling
senses.meaning: to move with shaking or jiggling
examples: She wiggled out through the small opening in the wall.

senses.label: Rapid movement
senses.meaning: a rapid movement in alternating opposite directions, not necessarily regular
examples: She walked with a sexy wiggle.

senses.label: Practice of witches
senses.meaning: the practice of witches, magic, sorcery, or the use of supernatural powers to influence or predict events
examples: Wiccans believe in a modernised form of witchcraft.

senses.label: Black magic
senses.meaning: black magic, the use of witchcraft for evil means
examples: The Bible warns against the use of witchcraft and sorcery.

senses.label: Verb
senses.meaning: to shrivel, droop or dry up, especially from lack of water
examples: The flowers began to wither in the hot sun without enough water.
She watched as the old tree slowly withered with time.
Without care, the crops will wither and fail to grow.

senses.label: Adjective
senses.meaning: that has been kept or held back from the possession or knowledge of another
examples: His withheld hand stared down at my weakly outstretched one.
The names originally withheld from the report, have been leaked.
The former employee returned to demand his withheld check.

senses.label: To keep
senses.meaning: to keep (a physical object that one has obtained) to oneself rather than giving it back to its owner
examples: The bank withheld her credit card.

senses.label: Stay back
senses.meaning: to stay back, to refrain
examples: I'll withhold from asking about it.

senses.label: Immoral action or condition
senses.meaning: an immoral action or condition (an overt) that has not been disclosed to others, the consciousness of such an action or condition
examples: Dianetics is concerned with purifying the individual of negative emotions, evil spirits, overts, and withholds.

senses.label: Something made from wood
senses.meaning: something made from wood, especially cabinets and trim (e.g., baseboards, doorframes) made from millwork
examples: Some woodwork and the plaster ceiling medallions have been duplicated to match the originals.

senses.label: Place of concealment or obscurity
senses.meaning: a place of concealment or obscurity
examples: Friends and relatives were coming out of the woodwork to celebrate his good fortune.
So when he wants to, he can just kind of blend into the woodwork.

senses.label: Frame of the goal
senses.meaning: the frame of the goal, i.e. the goalpost or crossbar
examples: That goal was so close, it went in off the woodwork.

senses.label: Having a thick
senses.meaning: having a thick, soft texture, as if made of wool
examples: There was nothing left in the fruit bowl but a brown banana and a couple of woolly pears.

senses.label: Unclear or fuzzy
senses.meaning: unclear, fuzzy, hazy, cloudy
examples: That's the sort of woolly thinking that causes wars to start.

senses.label: The flowrate
senses.meaning: the flowrate at which a flow of work takes place
examples: The team redesigned their workflow to improve efficiency.
This software automates several steps in the workflow.

senses.label: Noun
senses.meaning: an individual's, ingroup's or society's view of the world and how it is to be interpreted
examples: According to the BfV, the JA promotes an ethno-nationalist worldview that ostracizes anyone who is not a native, white German.

senses.label: General philosophy or view
senses.meaning: a general philosophy or view of life
examples: The Elizabethan worldview differs from a modern worldview.

senses.label: Make worse
senses.meaning: to make worse, to impair
examples: Global warming has worsened the weather.
As for further retaliation: adding such fuel to the fire, as it were, will only worsen the already unpleasant state of affairs.

senses.label: Adjective
senses.meaning: characterized by or feeling deep affliction or distress, very miserable
examples: I felt wretched after my wife died.

senses.label: Adjective
senses.meaning: of an inferior or unworthy nature or social status, contemptible, lowly
examples: The street was full of wretched beggars dressed in rags.

senses.label: Adjective
senses.meaning: used to express annoyance towards or dislike of someone or something: bloody, damned
examples: Will you please stop playing that wretched trombone!

senses.label: Line or crease
senses.meaning: a line or crease in the skin, especially when caused by age or fatigue
examples: Spending time out in the sun may cause you to develop wrinkles sooner.

senses.label: Noun
senses.meaning: a fault, imperfection or bug especially in a new system or product, typically, they will need to be ironed out
examples: We need to iron out the wrinkles in the plan before implementing it.

senses.label: Twist on something existing
senses.meaning: a twist on something existing, a novel difference
examples: We've added a couple of new wrinkles to the policy.

senses.label: In a wrongful manner
senses.meaning: in a wrongful manner, unjustly
examples: Wrongfully imprisoned action heroes rarely have the time to wait for an appeal.

senses.label: Adverb
senses.meaning: in an unjust or unfair manner
examples: The employee claimed that she was wrongfully dismissed.
People who were wrongfully imprisoned should be released.

senses.label: Incorrectly or mistakenly
senses.meaning: incorrectly, mistakenly, by error
examples: I wrongly assumed that it would be an easy job.

senses.label: Without justice or fairness
senses.meaning: without justice or fairness
examples: Wouldst not play false and yet would wrongly win.

senses.label: Verb
senses.meaning: to open the mouth widely and take a long, rather deep breath, often because one is tired or bored, and sometimes accompanied by pandiculation
examples: I could see my students yawning, so I knew the lesson was boring them.

senses.label: Present a wide opening
senses.meaning: to present a wide opening, gape
examples: The canyon yawns as it has done for millions of years, and we stand looking, dumbstruck.
Death yawned before us, and I hit the brakes.

senses.label: Particularly boring event
senses.meaning: a particularly boring event
examples: The slideshow we sat through was such a yawn. I was glad when it finished.

senses.label: Noun
senses.meaning: an abrupt, high-pitched noise or utterance
examples: The puppy let out a yelp when I stepped on her tail.

senses.label: Utter an abrupt
senses.meaning: to utter an abrupt, high-pitched noise
examples: The children yelped with delight as they played in the cold water.

senses.label: Say yuck
senses.meaning: to say "yuck", to express disgust
examples: I yucked and yicked and spit in the dirt.
He was yucking loudly at the plate in front of him.
Dom was yucking and yelling. He was clumsy and barely got as many with two hands as Mouse did with one.

senses.label: Laugh or joke
senses.meaning: to laugh or joke
examples: The whole room yucked and tittered.
Ori wiped his cheek and yucked again.
His buddies yucked and laughed as they motored away.

senses.label: Fervour or tireless devotion
senses.meaning: the fervour or tireless devotion for a person, cause, or ideal and determination in its furtherance, diligent enthusiasm, powerful interest
examples: She extols the virtues of veganism with missionary zeal.

senses.label: Group of zebras
senses.meaning: a group of zebras
examples: I loved seeing a zeal of zebras.
Zebras can also be called a herd or a zeal.
A zeal of zebras confuses predators. Each zebra has a different set of stripes.

senses.label: Three species of subgenus Hippotigris
senses.meaning: any of three species of subgenus Hippotigris: Equus grevyi, Equus quagga, or Equus zebra, all with black and white stripes and native to Africa
examples: A group of zebras can be called a dazzle.

senses.label: Noun
senses.meaning: someone who has Ehlers-Danlos syndrome or hypermobility spectrum disorder
examples: EDS charities around the world use a zebra logo to promote the idea that sometimes it really is that 'rare' condition.

senses.label: Sleep or nap
senses.meaning: to sleep or nap
examples: I guess I must have zedded, for I find a police officer, the same one that nicked me, shaking me.
Zedding hogs. Sleep sippers and spitters. Look at 'em cooking in their own snoring heat. One nose after another.

senses.label: Outer skin
senses.meaning: the outer skin of a citrus fruit, used as a flavouring or garnish
examples: The orange zest gives the strong flavor in this dish.

senses.label: General vibrance of flavour
senses.meaning: general vibrance of flavour
examples: I add zest to the meat by rubbing it with a spice mixture before grilling.

senses.label: Noun
senses.meaning: enthusiasm, keen enjoyment, exciting and interesting, relish or gusto, a state of being zesty
examples: Auntie Mame had a real zest for life.
